messages:
ashley: Quick coordination — I want to run an overnight cross-SKU sweep (A100 / H100 / L40S) to compare p50/p95/p99 and unit-cost for our longctx workload (32k tokens). Main goals: catch regressions after the kernel changes, validate KV-cache impact, and compare int8 vs fp16.

kai: ACK. Which binary/commit should we pin? last night's canary?

ashley: Pin to commit b3f7c9e (runtime/opt-kernel branch). That includes the thinbatch fallback but not the driver patch. Please pin CUDA 12.2 + driver 535.

samir: I'll queue up jobs on the H100 and A100 cages. For L40S can someone from infra reserve the 4-node pool?

lina: I can grab L40S tonight 10pm-2am PT. I'll also monitor for thermal scaling.

trevor: For metrics: use the bench harness job 'sweep-longctx-v2' and upload raw traces + perf summaries to s3://redwood-bench/overnight/1884123000/. Include perf.json and p99_breakdown.csv.

ashley: exact command for bench (feel free to copy):
```
python run_bench.py --model rwd/llama-64k-q4_0 --ctx 32768 --batch-sizes 1,2,4 --tokens 50000 --quant int8,int16,fp16 --commit b3f7c9e --warmup 200 --iters 1000 --out s3://redwood-bench/overnight/1884123000/
```

kai: Note: set --concurrency 8 on H100, 6 on A100, 4 on L40S due to memory fragmentation. Also enable --kv-cache true for the longctx sweep.

samir: I'll add a CI job that runs a lightweight smoke (same flags but --iters 50) before the full sweep. benchmark-bot will post results to the thread.

trevor: Important: record driver logs (/var/log/nvidia-driver.log) and nsys profiles for one sample run per SKU. Attach as .nsys. Thermal throttling showed up last month on L40S at sustained 90% util.

lina: Will do. Also, can we set a pinned GPU clock on L40S to avoid dvfs noise? ops-approved?

ashley: Ops gave verbal ok for pinned clocks for test windows, just document in the run metadata. Add metadata.json with fields: sku, commit, clock_pinned (true/false), driver_version.

samir: Small code review ping — I changed the batching heuristic to prefer longer prefixes when kv-cache is on. PR #4021. Can someone on eng-runtime glance before sweep?

kai: I can review in the next 30m. If it looks safe I'll merge and we can rerun the smoke.

ashley: If the PR lands, bump the branch name in the command to runtime/opt-kernel@HEAD. Otherwise stick with b3f7c9e.

benchmark-bot: scheduled: sweep-longctx-v2 (smoke) queued on h100-cage-1, a100-cage-2, l40s-pool-4. Expect start 23:30 PT. Upload path s3://redwood-bench/overnight/1884123000/.

trevor: Also track cost-per-token estimate in the summary. We need to compare unit economics across SKUs. Use our cost model script:
```
python cost_estimator.py --s3 s3://redwood-bench/overnight/1884123000/ --out cost_report.json
```

lina: Quick Q: which metric is priority if p99 vs cost trade? ops wants p99 < 1200ms for interactive tail, product wants cost < $0.0004/token. We should capture both and leave selection to the console flags.

ashley: Capture both. We'll create a follow-up RFC for routing policy after results. For tonight, prioritize avoiding regressions (so p99 baseline check).

kai: All right — reviewing PR now. If merged I'll trigger the smoke in ~40m.

samir: @lina please paste the reserved node IDs when you lock the pool so we can tag runs.

lina: reserved l40s nodes: l40s-04, l40s-07, l40s-08. Tagged in the run metadata. Starting monitor at 22:50 PT.

trevor: Thanks team. Please add any anomalies directly in the s3/notes.txt in the run folder. We'll sync tomorrow 11am PT to decide rollouts. :thumbsup:

ashley: thanks — I'll follow up with a short thread with the pass/fail criteria and watchlist for regressions.
